title: Slack bridge: relay kith chats to/from Slack channels and DMs
description:
A standalone bridge process that relays messages bidirectionally between kith and Slack. Runs on any host with tailnet access to the user's kithd. No central server; the bridge is operated by the kith user.

Architecture:
- Bridge process holds Slack app credentials (bot token) and kithd JMAP credentials
- Slack → kith: receive Slack events via Events API (HTTP push) or Socket Mode (WebSocket, no public URL needed); call kithd Message/set create
- kith → Slack: subscribe to kithd EventSource; on new message call Slack Web API chat.postMessage
- Each bridged Slack channel/DM maps to a kith chat ID (stored in bridge config or SQLite)
- Identity: Slack messages appear in kith attributed to a synthetic contact; kith messages appear in Slack as bot posts with sender name prefix (e.g. 'alice: hello')
- Attachments: upload to Slack via files.uploadV2; download from Slack and forward to kithd blob upload

Scope:
- Bridge config file: kithd URL, bot token, channel→chatId mapping
- Socket Mode preferred (no public ingress required — fits tailnet-only deployments)
- Message deduplication (avoid echo loops)
- Graceful reconnect on EventSource or WebSocket drop
- Target: Rust binary (fits kith's single-static-binary ethos) or small Go binary
- Distribution: same release artifact as kithd; systemd service unit included

Key decisions for research phase:
- Socket Mode vs Events API (public URL) — Socket Mode preferred for no-ingress deployments
- Per-user bot (personal Slack app) vs shared app requiring Slack admin approval
- How to handle Slack threads vs kith replyTo
